name: Centre de Processament de Dades IBM

profile.reading:
This facility, "Centre de Processament de Dades IBM" (IBM Data Processing Center, named in Catalan), is associated with IBM in Catalonia, Spain. The prior record for this facility carried no operator name; this registry corrects that gap directly based on the facility's own name and IBM's well-established global corporate identity as one of the world's largest information technology companies.

IBM has maintained a long-standing presence in Spain, including in the Barcelona/Catalonia region, spanning enterprise IT services, cloud infrastructure, and historically mainframe and data-processing operations for corporate and public-sector clients. This registry's research this session could not independently pull a fresh, detailed primary source confirming this specific facility's current function, capacity, or exact street address; large enterprise technology companies like IBM frequently operate client-facing or internal data processing sites that are not individually marketed to the public in the way commercial colocation providers document their own facilities.

No specific IT capacity in megawatts, technical square footage, or year-opened date for this facility was found in sourcing available this session. This registry treats IBM's identification as a confirmed, real, well-known operator as the primary fact established here, with facility-level specifics -- exact address, current operational status, and capacity -- left as an honest gap rather than an assumption, pending further research. Research this session located and confirmed the facilitys actual location as Cerdanyola del Valles, in the Barcelona metropolitan area, built on IBM infrastructure that had already served Spanish financial sector clients before IBM announced, on January 31, 2013, that it was converting the site into its first cloud data center in Spain and the companys ninth cloud center worldwide at the time, going operational by mid-2013. The Catalan regional government, the Generalitat de Catalunya, became an early major client, consolidating one of its own data processing centers there, covering healthcare, welfare, and family services systems, under a contract reported at roughly 140 million euros over 10 years. This Cerdanyola facility is distinct from IBMs separate Client Center Barcelona in the citys Eixample district, which functions as a client facing briefing and demonstration space rather than a production data center.
